observation_summary: The FastMath.cosh and FastMath.sinh methods incorrectly returned Infinity for large input values because they used an intermediate exp(x) calculation that overflowed, even when the final result should have been representable.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the computational strategy for calculating cosh and sinh when the input is large. Instead of directly calculating 0.5 * exp(x), which overflows, the code now uses a more robust mathematical approach (splitting the exponentiation) to avoid intermediate overflow. This is a correction to the internal procedural logic of the method, fitting the definition of Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'This is due to using exp( x )/2 for values of |x| above 20: the result sometimes should not overflow, but exp( x ) does, so we end up with some infinity.'
The fix_diff_oracle shows the introduction of a new conditional check and a different mathematical formula: 'final double t = exp(0.5 * x); return (0.5 * t) * t;'
The fix modifies the internal computation logic of the cosh and sinh methods in FastMath.java.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check (if x >= LOG_MAX_VALUE), the primary purpose of this check is to enable a different, more robust computational algorithm to prevent overflow, rather than just validating input or preventing an error.
The fix is not about correcting a wrong constant or variable initialization, but about changing the mathematical procedure used to compute the result.
